# The midpoint and radius of an interval, one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_mid_rad_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The midpoint $m$ and the radius $r$ of the interval $[x_l, x_u]$, with the values of `mid` and `rad` of IEEE 1788 for an unbounded or empty interval:

$$[m - r, m + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.midpoint()` | `Interval<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | $m$; computes the whole kernel, as the other does: `X.mid_rad()` gives both from one call; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `X.radius()` | `Interval<T, 1>` | `T` | $r$; computes the whole kernel, as the other does: `X.mid_rad()` gives both from one call; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `X.mid_rad()` | `Interval<T, 1>` | `MidRad<T, 1>` | $m$ and $r$ from one call; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $[x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- If $[x_l, x_u]$ is bounded: $m$ and $r$ are finite, $x_l \le m \le x_u$, $\lvert m - \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert \le u\,\lvert \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert + \eta$, and $[m - r, m + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u]$: $r$ is the smallest number of `T` with that property, $\mathrm{RU}(\max(m - x_l, x_u - m))$.
- The whole line gives $m = 0$, $r = +\infty$; $[x_l, +\infty]$ with $x_l$ finite gives $m = \Omega$, the largest finite number of `T`, and $[-\infty, x_u]$ gives $m = -\Omega$, both with $r = +\infty$; the empty set gives two NaN. These are the values of `mid` and `rad` of IEEE 1788.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_mid_rad_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_mid_rad_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_mid_rad_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the sum of the halves, moved into the interval, and the larger directed distance to a bound (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_mid_rad_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_mid_rad_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`sub_up_1`](sub_up_1.md).

```
# The midpoint and the radius of an interval with one-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", "Midpoint, radius and the conversions"). For a bounded interval the midpoint is
# RN(RN(xl/2) + RN(xu/2)) moved into [xl, xu] if it fell outside (it can, by eta, when a halving
# underflows: for [eta, eta] both halves are zero), within u |(xl + xu)/2| + eta of the exact
# midpoint, and the radius is the larger of RU(m - xl) and RU(xu - m): the smallest number of T
# with [m - r, m + r] containing the interval. Halving first keeps [Omega, Omega] from
# overflowing. As in IEEE 1788: the whole line has midpoint 0, a half-line the largest finite
# number of its sign, both with radius +inf; the empty set gives two NaN.

om = pred(const inf)
mo = neg(om)
ml = lt(xl, mo)
l  = select(ml, mo, xl)
mu = lt(om, xu)
h  = select(mu, om, xu)
hl = prod(l, const up(1/2))
hu = prod(h, const up(1/2))
ma = add(hl, hu)
ca = lt(ma, l)
mb = select(ca, l, ma)
cb = lt(h, mb)
mc = select(cb, h, mb)
ra = sub_up_1(mc, l)
rb = sub_up_1(h, mc)
rm = lt(ra, rb)
rc = select(rm, rb, ra)
md = select(ml, mo, mc)
me = select(mu, om, md)
bo = and(ml, mu)
mf = select(bo, 0, me)
un = or(ml, mu)
rd = select(un, const inf, rc)
ne = lt(xl, const inf)
m  = select(ne, mf, const nan)
r  = select(ne, rd, const nan)
```
